Session amc confirmed.
conviction_note: The findings sum to a small positive (+1.6). The stock has already been de-rated 23% in 20 sessions on a sector-wide AI-semis sell-off, the Street's Q4 bar (~$223M, +3.5% q/q) looks undemanding against management's own 'no stairstep / orders cover next year / 26-28 week lead times' commentary, and the inventory/WIP build corroborates the ramp. Against that, this name has fallen after 5 of its last 7 prints, including -21.5% on a strong beat-and-raise in July, there is mild put skew (+3.8 vol pts), and the open Silicon Motion award (claim $160M+ vs $65M unrestricted cash) is a fat left tail. So p_up is only 52, on an abs move of 12% (the name's median reaction is 12.6%; the 7.06% option-netted event move looks understated against 7 of 7 prior reactions above 9.9%). The scaled number (+0.48) is much smaller than the findings sum (+1.6) because the reaction function (beats sold) gets veto power over the fundamental lean.

Consensus $214.95M revenue / $0.56 non-GAAP EPS (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/MXL/earnings/), with Benzinga at about $211.2M / $0.51 (snippet only, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/MXL/earnings-forecasts). The guide and two sources roughly agree, so the bar is sourced. Q4 2026 consensus is about $222.6M revenue (Benzinga snippet only, single source, unverified). EarningsWhispers' $171.6M is stale (pre-guide) and is disowned. The last 6 quarters' revenue beats ran 0-2.6% (MarketBeat table).
positioning_check: Short interest 4.89M shares, 5.84% of float, 1.49 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement. It has risen 5 reports running (4.17M at 7/31) but is not crowded (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/MXL/short-interest/). Skew is +3.82 vol pts (downside paid, mild); put/call OI 0.67. The stock is down 16.4% in 5 days, 23.4% in 20 days and 49% off its 52-week high, into a sector sell-off (SOX about -12% in the week to 10-14 on Broadcom/Intel CEO capital warnings). Insiders: CEO Seendripu sold about 591k shares (~$50M) over 6 months, with Forms 4 on 2026-08-18 and 2026-09-01; FMR cut 68.6% in Q2.

findings.finding: The Street's Q4 2026 revenue bar is about $222.6M, only +3.5% q/q on a ~$215M Q3. Management's own forward commentary points above that: on the Q2 call it said there would be no 'stairstep', with optical volumes rising as more customers enter production and visibility of about six months, and Q1-27 orders already being placed. At Citi TMT (scheduled 2026-09-09) it said customer orders/forecasts cover next year, lead times are 26-28 weeks and pricing stays firm through end-2027. The 10-Q shows inventory +35% to $105.5M, with WIP up from $47.6M to $79.0M since December, plus restricted cash tied to purchase obligations. This corroborates a ramp rather than a stall, so a Q4 guide midpoint in the $230-240M area would clear the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is what moves this name. April 2026: Q2 guide well above Street, +76.1%. July 2026: Q3 guide of $210-220M against ~$175M Street still fell -21.5%, after a ~22% run into the print. So a strong guide has paid once and been sold once. 5 of the last 7 reactions were down.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q4 consensus of +3.5% q/q sits far below the Q2-to-Q3 step (+27%) and below management's 'continued rise' language. If the market expected a big Q4 step, the 20-day tape would not show -23% into the print, and the event-implied move would not be netted down to 7%. However, the Q4 consensus figure is single-source (Benzinga snippet), so this is capped.
findings.independence: 10-Q inventory/WIP build (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1288469/000128846926000051/mxl-20260630.htm, 2026-07-23) and the Citi TMT summary (https://quartr.com/events/maxlinear-inc-mxl-citi-s-2026-global-tmt-conference_ozX1H5eK; conference scheduled 2026-09-09 per the company's 2026-08-17 release, Quartr labels it 2026-10-06). Q4 consensus is from Benzinga (snippet). Caveat: at Citi, management reiterated the FY optical midpoint of $220M rather than raising it, which limits the optical upside.

findings.finding: MXL goes into this print after a sector-driven de-rating rather than a run-up. It is -16.4% over 5 days and -23.4% over 20 days. The cause is a sector-wide sell-off: optical names fell on 10-15 ('rotation into defensives', no company news), and the SOX fell ~12% in the week to 10-14 after Broadcom's Hock Tan and Intel's Lip-Bu Tan said capital, not chips, is AI's constraint, while Hock Tan said demand exceeds supply through 2029. In July, by contrast, the stock ran ~22% into the print and fell 21.5% on a beat-and-raise. No MXL-specific negative 8-K, PR or downgrade appears since July 23 (EDGAR shows only Forms 4/144/13G).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: up ~22% into the print, then -21.5% on beat-and-raise. April 2026: entered depressed and moved +76%. That is two observations consistent with run-in mattering, which is not a base rate.
findings.why_not_priced: The de-rating is the price. The claim is about the reaction function: a lower bar into a print where the company-level demand commentary has not changed. If the market had priced a demand problem at MXL specifically, short interest would be building faster (it is +1% in the last report, DTC 1.5) and skew would be steeper than +3.8 vol pts.
findings.independence: Broadcom/Intel CEO remarks, 2026-10-12 (https://finviz.com/news/401102/broadcom-ceo-sees-capital-as-main-constraint-on-ai-growth-despite-easing-chip-shortages); Quiver 2026-10-12 says the -6.9% day had no company-specific news (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/MaxLinear+Slides+as+Recent+Rally+Loses+Steam+Ahead+of+Earnings). This is an inference about reaction, not a company number.

findings.finding: Optical counterparties that reported after MXL last spoke (2026-07-23) describe continuing strong demand. Credo's FQ1-27 (reported 2026-09-02, quarter ended 2026-08-01) had revenue of $479M (+115% y/y), a record optical DSP quarter and a guide of $525-535M. Eoptolink's H1 report (2026-08-25) had Q2 revenue +50.8% q/q, and brokers cite high Q3/Q4 order visibility. Neither shows an air pocket in 800G module/DSP demand during MXL's Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MXL has beaten revenue consensus by 0-2.6% in each of the last 6 quarters (MarketBeat), and the reactions to those beats were mostly negative.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced. It rules out a demand-collapse reading of the 23% drawdown rather than adding new upside. These are proxies: Credo competes with MXL, and module makers are customers but unnamed.
findings.independence: Eoptolink H1 2026 (https://m.c114.com.cn/w123-1316262.html, 2026-08-25). It is a different company and document, but the same industry proxy.

findings.finding: The Silicon Motion SIAC arbitration (claim: $160M termination fee plus further damages) has had its hearings concluded (October 2025 and March 2026), and the parties are awaiting a final award. One call summary expected a decision in 2H 2026. MXL had $64.8M of unrestricted cash, a $125M term loan and negative H1 operating cash flow (-$4.1M) at 6/30. An adverse award disclosed in the Q3 release or 10-Q would force a financing question. No award has been reported by either party as of 10-22, so this is a low-probability tail inside the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There has been no award in the history. The matter has been a disclosed risk factor since 2023.
findings.why_not_priced: Arbitration is confidential under SIAC rules, so an award could sit undisclosed until a periodic filing. The market is not visibly pricing a $160M+ charge against a $6bn market cap with $65M cash: skew is only +3.8 vol pts.
findings.independence: MXL 10-Q liquidity figures (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1288469/000128846926000051/mxl-20260630.htm, 2026-07-23) and the SIMO FY2025 20-F (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001329394/000119312526197184/d17718d20f.htm). Same matter, so this is one finding.

findings.finding: The CEO sold about 591k shares (~$50M) in the 6 months to October, with Forms 4 filed 2026-08-18 and 2026-09-01 after Form 144s on 8/14 and 8/17. Insiders made 25 sales and 0 purchases. FMR cut its stake 68.6% in Q2.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: these are public Forms 4. It is filed because it bears on how holders read a beat.
findings.independence: EDGAR filing index for CIK 1288469 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001288469&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40) lists the Forms 4 and 144.

findings.finding: The Q3 non-GAAP gross margin guide is 58.5-61.5% (midpoint 60% vs 59.5% in Q2). Management flagged higher wafer, test and packaging costs, only partly passed on, plus premiums paid for supply in a tight market. Mix is favourable, since infrastructure carries above-average margins. The risk is a print at the low end of the GM range even on a revenue beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: commentary cited margin pressure in the -21.5% reaction (Chartmill/business-news-today coverage).
findings.why_not_priced: It lands inside the company's guided range, so it is mostly expected and sized toward 0.

baseline_tension: Mild tension: the small positive lean cuts against the +3.8 vol-pt put skew and against the name's habit of selling prints (5 of 7 down), but it agrees with the 23% pre-print de-rating having lowered the bar. So p_up sits at 52, not higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; this name sold 5 of 7 prints, including a July beat-and-raise): Q4 guide finding 1.5 -> 1.2; p_up 53 -> 52
Lesson 5 (inference/proxy sized small): pre-print de-rating finding 1.5 -> 1.0, as it is a reaction inference, not a company number; peer-demand proxy 0.5 -> 0.3
Lesson 6 (inside the guided range -> toward 0): GM-cost finding -0.3 -> -0.2
Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest checked (5.8% float, DTC 1.5, not crowded); insider-selling finding -0.3 -> -0.2 as public and largely priced
Lesson 2 (one-off): Silicon Motion award kept at -0.5 with a wide range, because it has a path to financing/the multiple given $65M cash vs a $160M+ claim
